## Kyoto 5-Day Slow-Travel Plan
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg

A relaxed Kyoto itinerary for 2 adults, centered on temples, local food, and one easy day trip. It keeps transit simple, leaves room for breaks, and targets an estimated total under **$1,500** excluding flights.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary and Budget
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/calendar.svg

Day 1: Higashiyama Welcome Walk
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Arrive, check in, and take a gentle walk through **Gion** and **Higashiyama**.
- Afternoon: Visit **Kiyomizu-dera** and nearby lanes like Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka.
- Dinner: Kaiseki-lite or set meal near Gion; keep it simple and early.
- Rainy-day backup: **Kyoto National Museum** or a long café stop in central Kyoto.
- Transit: JR/subway + local bus; avoid taxis unless needed.
- Estimated cost for 2: **$220–$280**

Day 2: Arashiyama Temple Circuit
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Go early to **Tenryu-ji** and the **Bamboo Grove** before crowds build.
- Afternoon: Cross to **Okochi Sanso Garden** or stroll the river area at an easy pace.
- Dinner: Tofu-focused dinner or soba in Arashiyama.
- Rainy-day backup: **Saga-Arashiyama area cafés** and **Togetsukyo** short indoor pauses between stops.
- Transit: JR to Saga-Arashiyama or Hankyu/Randen depending on where you stay.
- Estimated cost for 2: **$200–$260**

Day 3: Central Kyoto Temples and Markets
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
- Morning: Visit **Nishiki Market** for breakfast bites and light shopping.
Media: Alt=Morning: Visit **Nishiki Market** for breakfast bites and light shopping, Kyoto, Japan
- Afternoon: Explore **Nijo Castle** and one nearby temple such as **Shoren-in** or **Chion-in**.
- Dinner: Izakaya or noodle dinner in the downtown area.
- Rainy-day backup: Spend more time at **Nishiki Market** and add a department-store food floor.
- Transit: Subway + short walks; this is one of the easiest low-stress days.
- Estimated cost for 2: **$180–$240**

Day 4: Day Trip to Nara
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/signpost-split.svg
- Morning: Take the train to **Nara** and visit **Todai-ji** early.
- Afternoon: Walk through **Nara Park** and, if energy is good, add **Kasuga Taisha**.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/25/DeerNaraJapan.jpg Alt=Afternoon: Walk through **Nara Park** and, if energy is good, add **Kasuga Taisha**, Kyoto, Japan
- Dinner: Return to Kyoto for a calm dinner near Kyoto Station or downtown.
- Rainy-day backup: Stay closer to **Todai-ji Museum** and indoor temple spaces, then shorten the park time.
Media: Alt=Rainy-day backup: Stay closer to **Todai-ji Museum** and indoor temple spaces, then shorten the park time, Kyoto, Japan
- Transit: JR or Kintetsu rail round trip; no car needed.
- Estimated cost for 2: **$170–$230**

Day 5: Fushimi Inari and Farewell Food Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/moon-stars.svg
- Morning: Start early at **Fushimi Inari Taisha** and do a partial uphill walk, not the full loop.
- Afternoon: Relax with a slow lunch, then visit **Tofuku-ji** if you want one final temple stop.
- Dinner: Final Kyoto meal — ramen, yakitori, or a nicer tempura set depending on budget.
- Rainy-day backup: Replace the hike with **Tofuku-ji** grounds and a long lunch/café afternoon.
- Transit: JR Nara Line or Keihan line depending on your base.
- Estimated cost for 2: **$180–$250**

## Budget Check for 2 Adults
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/currency-rupee.svg

- Lodging, 4 nights: **$520–$760**
- Local transit: **$45–$80**
- Temple/castle admissions: **$35–$70**
- Food and drinks: **$480–$620**
- Day trip to Nara: **$40–$70**
- Buffer for snacks, souvenirs, rainy-day extras: **$80–$120**

Estimated total: **$1,200–$1,420**
This stays under your **$1,500** target with room for a nicer meal or upgraded hotel.

## Best Pace and Transit Approach
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/car-front.svg

- Base yourself near **Kyoto Station**, **Gion**, or **Shijo** for easy subway/bus access.
- Use trains first, buses second; Kyoto buses can be crowded.
- Start temple visits early, then keep afternoons lighter with food stops and short walks.
- Book one hotel and avoid moving luggage mid-trip.

## Quick Actions

- Kyoto transit overview: https://www.visitsightseeing.com/japan/kyoto
- Nara day trip context: https://www.japan-guide.com/e/e2165.html
